classification.difficultyReason: Development: coordinate the same books-read category across two representations, decode four pictograph symbols using the two-friends key, read the column frequency, and compare the resulting counts.

content.prompt: How many more of Clive’s friends read 3–4 books in the last month than Alvin’s friends?

spec.description: Native bordered four-row pictograph with outlined upright books, spine/page details and a clipped half-book. The key remains above the symbol column. Decorative cell and book shading is omitted.
spec.mathematics: One full book represents 2 friends. Top-to-bottom categories 5+, 3–4, 1–2, 0 contain 2, 4, 1.5 and 2 book symbols, respectively.
spec.answerVisibility: The key and every source symbol, including the half-book, are supplied question data.

spec.description: Four separated columns with an integer vertical scale, horizontal grid, both axis titles and source category order. White column interiors mask gridlines.
spec.mathematics: Books-read categories 0, 1–2, 3–4 and 5+ have frequencies 5, 3, 2 and 5. The vertical scale is 0–8 in intervals of 1.
spec.answerVisibility: All columns and labels are supplied data; no comparison answer is included.

answer.worked:
For 3–4 books:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Clive's friends}&=4\times2\\&=8\\\text{Alvin's friends}&=2\\\text{Difference}&=8-2\\&=6\end{align*}$$
Clive has $6$ more friends in this category.
